items.content:
Dear Pathfinders,

The Polaris Institute plans to carry out server maintenance for an update on November 12, 2026. You will be unable to log in during maintenance, so please plan your adventures accordingly.

Here is a preview of what’s coming in this update!

I. Maintenance Schedule

\

"Aniimo-Europe" 2026/11/12 06:00 ~ 11:00 UTC+0

"Aniimo-Americas" 2026/11/12 02:00 ~ 07:00 UTC-4

"Aniimo-Apac" 2026/11/12 14:00 ~ 19:00 UTC+8

\ Glimmer × 500

\ Pathfinders who registered before the Season 2 version update

※The actual maintenance duration may vary depending on progress. Thank you for your understanding. Once maintenance is complete, please restart the game client to ensure that you are running the latest version.

II. New Content Preview

New Story Quests

\

Two new Journey Quests will be added to Crescent Bay:

1. "The Coral Sea of Dreams": Reefish is always dreaming of a distant, tranquil coral sea. A paradise reachable only by crossing tidal storms—why have you chosen this fish, and how can it find you?

2. "Squarrel’s Poem of Revolution": Chompy the Squarrel has been turning Mirrorsea Village upside down... She means well, of course... But how can we get her to settle down? Her human partner, Dora, may know something.

Major Feature Updates

\

\

Aniimo Affinity is now available. Increase an Aniimo’s Affinity level to unlock the following benefits:

1. Unlock the ability to rename that Aniimo.

2. Increase the effects of the active skills "Heal" and "Swoleshroom" on that Aniimo.

You can increase Aniimo Affinity in the following ways:

1. Place the Aniimo in your Party or Home to gradually gain Affinity.

2. Use the Star Up and Ascend features on the Aniimo.

3. Complete Pathfinder Challenges and take part in Operation: Egg Heist with the Aniimo.

4. Defeat wild Aniimo and Alphas in Idyll with the Aniimo.

※Each Aniimo has daily and weekly limits on Affinity gains. Please plan their development accordingly.

New Events

Prismana Snapshots

\

Phase 1: After the version update ~ 2026/11/16 03:59

"Aniimo-Europe" After the version update ~ 2026/11/16 03:59 UTC+0

"Aniimo-Americas" After the version update ~ 2026/11/16 03:59 UTC-4

"Aniimo-Apac" After the version update ~ 2026/11/16 03:59 UTC+8

Phase 2: 2026/11/16 04:00 ~ 2026/11/23 03:59

"Aniimo-Europe" 2026/11/16 04:00 ~ 2026/11/23 03:59 UTC+0

"Aniimo-Americas" 2026/11/16 04:00 ~ 2026/11/23 03:59 UTC-4

"Aniimo-Apac" 2026/11/16 04:00 ~ 2026/11/23 03:59 UTC+8

Phase 3: 2026/11/23 04:00 ~ 2026/11/30 03:59

"Aniimo-Europe" 2026/11/23 04:00 ~ 2026/11/30 03:59 UTC+0

"Aniimo-Americas" 2026/11/23 04:00 ~ 2026/11/30 03:59 UTC-4

"Aniimo-Apac" 2026/11/23 04:00 ~ 2026/11/30 03:59 UTC+8

\

Be promoted to Student II.

\

1. Each phase features a designated Prismana Form Aniimo. Use the in-game camera to capture different Sparkling types of that phase’s target Aniimo and advance your snapshot progress.

2. \: In each phase, the first five different regular Sparkling types you capture each grant their respective photo rewards. Capture five different types in total to claim an additional reward. Capturing regular Sparkling types beyond those five grants no further progress or rewards.

3. \: Capture "Dazzling Sparkling" or "Shadow Sparkling" for the first time to claim the photo reward for that type. Capture either one to also claim an extra Special Snapshot reward, available once per phase. These special Sparkling types do not count toward the five types required for Regular Snapshots.

4. Taking another photo of the same Sparkling type grants no additional progress or duplicate rewards.

Aniimo Dash

Twine with your Aniimo and push your speed to the limit!

\

After the version update, the solo racing mode "Breezy Plains Cup - Full Throttle" will be available all day, while the multiplayer racing mode "Breezy Plains Cup - Speed Showdown" will be available daily from 18:00 to 24:00.

\

Track 1, Greenfield Shallows:

"Aniimo-Europe" After the version update ~ 2026/12/09 23:59 UTC+0

"Aniimo-Americas" After the version update ~ 2026/12/09 19:59 UTC-4

"Aniimo-Apac" After the version update ~ 2026/12/10 07:59 UTC+8

Track 2, Gullcove Cliffs:

"Aniimo-Europe" 2026/11/19 10:00 ~ 2026/12/09 23:59 UTC+0

"Aniimo-Americas" 2026/11/19 10:00 ~ 2026/12/09 19:59 UTC-4

"Aniimo-Apac" 2026/11/19 10:00 ~ 2026/12/10 07:59 UTC+8

Track 3, Redrock Trail:

"Aniimo-Europe" After the November 26 version update ~ 2026/12/09 23:59 UTC+0

"Aniimo-Americas" After the November 26 version update ~ 2026/12/09 19:59 UTC-4

"Aniimo-Apac" After the November 26 version update ~ 2026/12/10 07:59 UTC+8

\

Reach Pathfinder Level 40.

\

Aniimo Dash is an Aniimo racing competition held in Idyll. Twine with an Aniimo to take on racing challenges on designated tracks. You can set up your Party and prepare buffs before the race. Twining with certain Aniimo can trigger special events on the corresponding tracks. (Special events are currently unavailable on Redrock Trail in multiplayer racing mode.)

\

"Breezy Plains Cup - Full Throttle": Solo racing mode. Available all day, so you can take on a challenge at any time. Keep pushing yourself, beat your personal best, and aim for a higher rating!

"Breezy Plains Cup - Speed Showdown": Multiplayer racing mode. Available daily from 18:00 to 24:00, with up to 8 Pathfinders racing together.

During a race, compete for random item boxes and make clever use of the items you collect to battle other Pathfinders on the track!

\

Complete track missions to earn track-exclusive Designations, Profiles, avatar frames, development resources, and more.

New Outfits Arriving Soon

"Valiant Knight"

Wherever the blade points, a hero’s glory shines.

Visit "Shop" > "Recommended" to purchase the new "Valiant Knight" set.

"Shadow Rose"

A rose blooms in the dark of night, its thorns hidden in the moonlight.

Visit "Shop" > "Recommended" to purchase the new "Shadow Rose" set.

※These outfits will become available in batches after the version update.

III. Optimizations and Adjustments

Development Adjustments

1. Limited-Time Whirlbite Reset

\ The following Aniimo and its corresponding forms obtained before this balance adjustment: Whirlbite (Basic Form/Prismana Form)

\

Refunds all EXP Items used and reduces the corresponding EXP.

Star Up: Refunds all materials spent and resets to the initial state.

Capability Awakening: Refunds all materials spent and resets to the initial state.

Capafruit: Refunds the fruit, restores the number of available uses, and removes its effects.

\ 2026/11/12 04:00 ~ 2026/11/27 04:00

"Aniimo-Europe" 2026/11/12 04:00 ~ 2026/11/27 04:00 UTC+0

"Aniimo-Americas" 2026/11/12 04:00 ~ 2026/11/27 04:00 UTC-4

"Aniimo-Apac" 2026/11/12 04:00 ~ 2026/11/27 04:00 UTC+8

Story Experience

1. Added a voice playback feature to Story Review, allowing you to listen to a section’s story voice-over again.

2. Improved the display style of the information sidebar for quest markers on the map.

Homeland

1. Adjusted the opening times of the second and third phases of the seasonal Homeland events. They will now open after the version update.

2. Added collection rewards for furniture sets in the Index, and improved unlock requirement descriptions and display ordering in the Index.

3. Added HUD buttons for quickly returning from another player’s Park or Home to your own Park or Home.

4. Added voice-over to Homeland tutorial quests.

Operation: Egg Heist

1. Added an in-match report feature. Tap the button in the top-right corner of the screen to submit a report.

2. Added a display showing the names of enemy players Twined with a Giga-Egg.

3. Adjusted the level caps for Umbral Aniimo across all difficulty levels in Operation: Egg Heist Team Mode to make combat easier for lower-level players.

Mobile Optimizations

1. Added margin adjustment for frequently used control areas, allowing you to reposition them for a more comfortable experience.

2. Improved storage space checks and notifications on iOS.

3. Improved camera behavior in Catch Mode on mobile devices.

4. Improved the door-breaking effects in the Sanctum’s egg-heist gameplay to reduce stuttering.

IV. Bug Fixes

Aniimo and Combat

1. Fixed an issue where the clone created by Irisalis’s skill had a different model appearance from the original.

2. Fixed an issue where Crocobask’s Ultimate could occasionally fail in sparring.

3. Fixed an issue where Ekrim’s skill could be interrupted unexpectedly on certain terrain.

4. Fixed an issue where the models of Sparkling Prismana Form Aniimo could occasionally display incorrectly.

5. Fixed an issue where Bubbeep could occasionally attack upon detecting a Pathfinder.

6. Fixed an issue with the incorrect icon for Dewple’s and Dewlop’s "Water Spray" skill.

7. Fixed an issue where the description of the buff granted by Pouchwisp’s Ultimate displayed incorrectly.

8. Fixed an issue with incorrect avatar icons for non-Basic Form Dewlop and Dewple.

9. Fixed an issue where the cooldown of Pouchwisp’s "Coin Boost" skill was incorrect under certain circumstances.

10. Fixed an issue with incorrectly colored patches on the Sparkling Prismana Melloblum model.

11. Fixed an issue where Reefish and Coraliz could not correctly trigger the core effect of the "Omenbone Flute" Held Item when using "Coral Thicket".

12. Fixed an issue where Coraliz’s Element Level displayed incorrectly.

13. Fixed an issue where Glynsera failed to gain Ultimate Points correctly when using "Boomerang Blade" under certain circumstances.

14. Fixed an issue where gear durability in Operation: Egg Heist was not reduced correctly when Glynsera used "Boomerang Blade".

Map and Gameplay

1. Fixed an issue where some Lumin Marking map markers were not shown as complete after obtaining Amber.

2. Fixed an issue where the Pathfinder Challenge map markers did not match the challenge count for some accounts.

3. Fixed an issue where characters were not displayed on the "Star-Crossed Tea Party" vehicle.

Holo-Battle Sim

1. Fixed an issue where Holo-Battle Interlink star rewards could not be claimed manually under certain circumstances.

Operation: Egg Heist

1. Fixed an issue where opening a gold chest in "Operation: Egg Heist" caused the spawn-point marker to disappear.

2. Fixed an issue where impulse doors in "Operation: Egg Heist" could occasionally fail to break.

3. Fixed an issue where, in rare cases, an egg teleported back to the starting point after a player stopped Twining with it in "Operation: Egg Heist".

Homeland

1. Fixed an issue with abnormal self-illumination in the Homeland.

2. Fixed an issue where forced tracking was not applied to seasonal quests in the Homeland.

3. Fixed an issue where Aniimo in the Homeland could occasionally become stuck and stop working.

4. Fixed an issue where the outdoor Homeland decoration "Extra Large Panpanta" could not be sold.

5. Fixed an issue with the mobile layout of the Furniture Store interface.

6. Fixed an issue where Pathfinder information displayed incorrectly in private Parks.

7. Fixed an issue with the incorrect description of Mineral Sand.

8. Fixed an issue where Milled Rice, Premium Wheat, and other items were categorized incorrectly.

9. Fixed an issue where the pumpkin model had no collision.

10. Fixed an issue where some furniture was invisible on iOS.

11. Fixed an issue with abnormal outlines appearing in the Homeland.

12. Fixed an issue that prevented access to the second-floor RV.

13. Fixed an issue with clipping around the RV.

14. Fixed an issue with incorrect collision after resizing furniture.

15. Fixed an issue where some furniture models did not match their icons.

16. Fixed an issue where Sparkelf’s working state in the Homeland was incorrect.

17. Fixed an issue where the icons and models of some Homeland assets did not match.

18. Fixed an issue that could occasionally cause stuttering when entering the RV.

19. Fixed an issue where some furniture could not be resized.

Quests and Story

1. Fixed an issue where Journey Journal entries were not unlocked correctly after completing the corresponding story under certain circumstances.

Appearance

1. Fixed an issue where dye effects were not visible to other Pathfinders.

2. Fixed an issue where dyed hairstyles displayed incorrectly after saving.

Console Fixes

1. Fixed an issue that caused stuttering when sorting Aniimo on Xbox/PS5.

2. Fixed an issue that caused stuttering when releasing Aniimo on Xbox/PS5.

3. Fixed an issue where friends and mail were not displayed for some Pathfinders on Xbox/PS5.

4. Fixed an issue where the "Holo Training Ace" achievement name displayed incorrectly on Xbox/PS5.

5. Fixed an issue where some Pathfinders on PS5 could not retry logging in after login verification timed out and had to restart the game.

6. Fixed an issue where some Pathfinders on PS5 could not rejoin a party via an invitation or the system’s "Join Game" feature after leaving it.

7. Fixed an issue that caused stuttering when Jeburst launched water orbs after taking flight on Xbox/PS5.

8. Fixed an issue that could occasionally cause random crashes on PS5.

—Polaris Institute Operations Team

items.content:
To provide a better experience, Polaris Institute will continue to improve the game and address any issues identified. The fixes included in this update are as follows:

Bug Fixes

1. Fixed an issue in Operation: Egg Heist where wind could affect the Giga-Egg in unintended ways.

2. Fixed an issue where the "Nightborn Allure" outfit would clip through the character model after Pathfinders changed their body type.

3. Fixed an issue where a red notification dot in Elite Training would not clear.

4. Fixed a display issue with Nimbi in the Night Parade event.

5. Fixed an issue where teleporting after switching to a different Aniimo Storage Box would revert the box to its previous state.

6. Fixed an issue that prevented the "Holo Training Ace" achievement from unlocking after completing training on the highest difficulty in the current season.

7. Fixed an issue with dyeing the "Shadow of Phantom Night" hairstyle for male characters.

8. Fixed incorrect prompt text when interacting with a Bloom before its Branch was unlocked.

9. Fixed an issue in the main story "The Challenge of Fighting Upstream!" where players could climb a water column that was normally unclimbable.

10. Fixed an issue where some Aniimo spawned in the ground.

11. Fixed an issue where a puddle was not created when Sherro’s "Hydro Roll" was interrupted.

12. Fixed an issue where some Pathfinders’ nicknames appeared in the wrong color.

13. Fixed an issue that prevented players from switching between flying Aniimo during the Gravity Pull course.

14. Fixed an issue that prevented players from earning Windchaser Stamps through Stamp Rush even when they hadn’t reached the weekly limit.

15. Fixed display issues with some furniture in Home.

16. Fixed an issue where conflicting button assignments prevented players from selecting Aniimo emotes.

17. Fixed an issue that prevented players from reading lengthy in-game mail with a controller.

18. Fixed an issue that prevented players on PS5 from teaming up after receiving an invitation.

19. Fixed an issue where some buttons were missing from the Aniimo evolution screen.

Improvements and Adjustments

1. Steam and Epic Games players can now unlink their platform accounts under Settings > Account Settings.

2. Level 1 facilities can now use Season Recipes to produce items.

items.content:
Dear Pathfinders:

The sound of tides echoes, the distant isles are awakening, and the next stop of the journey has already arrived.

Polaris Institute plans to carry out a server maintenance update from 07:00 to 15:00 UTC+8 on October 29, 2026. During maintenance, you will not be able to log in to the game. Pathfinders, please plan your adventure time accordingly.

Below is an overview of this update. Please check it.

I. Maintenance Schedule

\

「Aniimo-Europe」2026/10/28 22:00~2026/10/29 7:00 (UTC+0)

「Aniimo-Americas」2026/10/28 19:00~2026/10/29 3:00 (UTC-4)

「Aniimo-Apac」2026/10/29 07:00~2026/10/29 15:00 (UTC+8)

\ 「Glimmer」× 500

\ Pathfinders who completed registration before the S2 season version update

※The actual duration of this maintenance may change depending on maintenance status. Thank you for your understanding. After maintenance is complete, please restart the game client to ensure the game is on the latest version.

II. New Content Preview

New Aniimo Debut

This version adds 51 brand-new Aniimo to the Idyll Continent. At the same time, Aniimo with multiple new Prismana Forms will appear across the world, awaiting Pathfinders' exploration and discovery~

\

Jeburst, Glameep, Pouchwisp, and Royalby—4 brand-new season-exclusive Prismana Aniimo. Don't miss them~

\

New Prismana Forms of Gachapus, Sugartini, Jabster, and Whirlbite appear in their corresponding areas across Whisperwake Isles, awaiting discovery and capture by Pathfinders.

\

Wind-element DPS Hypnyto joins the Idyll Continent—with the unique ability to control enemies to move along with itself, and can release small-area traps that deal continuous damage.

※Obtain Hypnyto and its Prismana Form through the Companion Handbook.

\

The Dark-element Breaker "Prismana Eklue," with both enemy-gathering and lifesteal DPS capabilities, officially debuts.

\

The first Pathfinder co-created Aniimo, Jaguaraun, a powerful and cool Lightning-element Breaker, is ready to set out!

New Map Region

As the adventure unfolds, Pathfinders will discover and set foot on the isolated Whisperwake Isles. This island cluster surrounded by the ocean has brand-new geography and is home to Aniimo of all shapes and forms. Here, Pathfinders can explore the interesting ecology and habits of Aniimo, catch new Aniimo as companions, open a new story chapter, and uncover the long-buried secrets of Whisperwake Isles.

Whisperwake Isles will open 4 map regions this time:

Crescent Bay—Giant bubbles like a crystalline dream gently embrace the lone tree in the middle of the lake. The Bubbeep family drifts leisurely by the lake surface of the moon bay. In the peaceful and relaxed Mirrorsea Village on the cliff, the islanders and Aniimo live together in harmony.

Rosy Mirelands—The river nourishes lush wetlands and woodlands. The wondrous slime of the Sugarfish family adds dreamy colors to the riverbanks, while also troubling other Aniimo living in the wetlands.

Wildwater Gorge—This is a gorge through which rushing rapids roar. Tempered by the currents, Aniimo full of power and energy live among the rapids and rocks. The Saws family rides the waves through the surging waters, while the Prawnch family treats this place as a natural training ground.

Cloudreach Falls—Lake water at the top of the cliff overflows from cracks, creating a spectacular waterfall. Beneath the huge drop of water, only Aniimo that never give up can climb the sky-reaching waterfall. Together with the Jeglid family, go upstream, explore the cliff covered by the waterfall, and keep climbing upward with the perseverance to reach the highest waterfall.

New Story Quests

\

Pathfinders will be guided by a wondrous song, swept into the waves, and arrive at the isolated Whisperwake Isles. Here, together with the little Aniimo Lyrelle and the youth Thesseo, begin a journey of pilgrimage and trials.

※After completing the prerequisite story quests, Whisperwake Isles-related content will automatically unlock.

\

New narrative-themed Journey Quests for Crescent Bay and Skytear Rift have been added, unfolding several warm little stories around the lives and bonds of Aniimo families such as Bubbeep, Salabask, Sugarfish, and Eko.

1. "Tale of Salabask Forest": The Salabask of Rosy Mirelands encounter a slime crisis, but their boss Lailai has turned into a talking Aniimo Egg? Pathfinders follow the trail and embark on an adventure to find the truth and friendship.

2. "The Rumored Seventh Princess": Princess, you are so beautiful, you are so kind, you are the most trusted friend of the Sugarfish, and the only star of the Guru Theater. Pathfinders are dragged into the performance in a daze—how will this messy Guru Theater end?

3. "Proof of the Rapids": According to the youth Thesseo, Skytear Rift has a legend of three challenges involving the rapids. How are these challenges completed, and where did they come from? Only truly powerful Pathfinders can find the answer.

4. "Who Moved the Golden Honey": Something big has happened—the golden honey of the Royalby has been stolen! Clever Pathfinder, there is only one truth!

5. "Itsy": The timid Lilipole Itsy doesn't dare to dance with everyone, doesn't dare to spray water to clean the mud, doesn't dare to... there are too many things it doesn't dare to do. How can it find courage...

\

1. "Coral Sea of Dreams": Reefish always loves to dream, and in its dreams there is a distant, peaceful coral sea. The ideal land that can only be reached by crossing tidal storms—why did you choose this fish, and how can the fish see you?

2. "Poem of Revolution": Many messy things have happened in Mirrorsea Village recently. Who is causing trouble? Or rather, who wants to make trouble...

3. "Ode to Tranquility": Della, the leader of the Dewlop family, wants to offer an "Ode to Tranquility" for the "Miracle of the Temple and the Great Tree," but this song has long been lost, and even Della herself cannot remember all of it. Pathfinders help collect the scattered melodies, complete the score, and uncover the story behind this song.

4. "Golden Treasure": Robin the Ekrim held a treasure hunt game, and the Eko played with great joy. But Robin's own treasure disappeared during the game...

\

New Journey Journal content related to Whisperwake Isles and Mirrorsea Village has been added. Pathfinders can unlock and view it by completing the related story quests.

New Growth Stage

Polaris Institute has taken note of the achievements made by Pathfinders. Dr. Lewis will contact Pathfinders at level 60 or higher to open new title promotion assessments: "Trailblazer II," "Trailblazer III," and Badge Challenges.

Elite Training unlocks the new "Chapter of Whisperwake." It can be challenged after the character's title reaches "Trailblazer I" and the Whisperwake Isles story quests have been advanced.

After title promotion, new character and Aniimo growth stages will be unlocked simultaneously:

1. "Trailblazer II": Aniimo level cap 60→65;

2. "Trailblazer III": Character level cap 65→70, Aniimo level cap 65→70.

3. Unlock new character Active Skills and Passive Talents.

Gameplay Season Update

"Operation: Egg Heist"

A new fair competitive PVP mode enters testing—3 teams compete for the Giga-Egg!

\ After the version update, daily 18:00 ~ 24:00

\

Character reaches level 50, Egg Heist rank reaches Rising Egg Scout

\

On a mysterious island, the dormant Giga-Egg awaits awakening! Three teams engage in fierce competition: fight for the sole Legendary Giga-Egg. Maintaining Twine with the Egg accumulates the Giga-Egg's activation value. When the Giga-Egg's activation value reaches 100% or the match ends, the team currently in Twine with the Giga-Egg wins. Victory is undecided until the final second—do your utmost to seize the Twine ownership of the Giga-Egg!

※This mode does not allow equipment loadouts to be configured or items to be brought in, and the stats of deployed Aniimo will be subject to balance adjustments.

※This gameplay is currently in testing and will be optimized and adjusted based on actual experience.

\

All members of the winning team will receive 1 "Giga-Egg," which guarantees an Umbral Egg and has a small chance to produce a Prismana Egg.

Each team that accumulates a certain activation value with the Giga-Egg can receive a reward Chest at the end, with a chance to produce season Collectibles.

\

Basic Collectibles:

1. Prismatic Iris: Among the gorgeous iris petals, prismatic colors sway. That brilliant thought rests gently in the soft embrace of the flower bud, peacefully awaiting the moment of bloom.

2. Butterfly Dream Amber: Treasured dreams flicker faintly within the crystal. Those irreplaceable moments have not faded in the slightest, as if even time cannot bear to flow on.

3. Ironhelm Shieldguard: Build fear into a solid wall, and turn cowardice into the courage to protect. The hardest enemy to defeat is always the timid self.

4. Songbird Serenade: The mountain wind whistles, the waves beat the rhythm, and the lonely gull has finally found companions. Bass and treble all take their places—the great gull choir begins!

Treasured Collectibles:

1. Collector’s Edition: Butterfly Dream Amber

2. Prismatic Iris · Sol

items.summary: Dear Pathfinders, We've heard a lot from you lately about Operation: Egg Heist, from Sanctum exploration and rescuing teammates to Chaos Mode's difficulty and Aniimo Training. We've been following your discussions closely and taking a fresh
items.content:
Dear Pathfinders,

We've heard a lot from you lately about Operation: Egg Heist, from Sanctum exploration and rescuing teammates to Chaos Mode's difficulty and Aniimo Training. We've been following your discussions closely and taking a fresh look at the gameplay experience to figure out what we can improve.

In this Dev Feedback, we're tackling some questions, sharing where things stand and what we're planning next.

Q1: Since the update, why does it feel like we're running into more Aniimo, and they're harder to shake off once they spot us? Why wasn't any of this mentioned in the patch notes?

First, we'd like to clear something up: we haven't made any numerical changes to things like Aniimo (or Chest) spawn probabilities. We're taking a close look at the spawning, combat disengagement, and enemy aggro issues you've reported to see if anything isn't working as intended. If we find a bug, we'll get it fixed as quickly as we can. It might also help to explain a little more about how Aniimo spawns work in the Sanctum. Not all Aniimo appear at the start of a run. As your exploration unfolds, more Aniimo may appear over time. When you dig up rare Aniimo Eggs or Rare Treasure, you disturb dormant Aniimo and attract them over! Any official changes to the game will be documented in our update announcements. We'll also make an effort to give you an earlier heads-up about major upcoming updates, so you know what to expect well in advance.

Q2: Whether you're down and calling for help or trying to rescue a teammate, the experience so far can be really frustrating. Are improvements on the way?

Absolutely! Exploring and fighting are a big part of Operation: Egg Heist, but having each other's backs should matter, too. We know the current rescue experience isn't quite where we'd like it to be, so we're planning new mechanics to make helping a downed teammate easier. We also want to give Pathfinders who go out of their way to help others some well-deserved recognition and rewards. Ultimately, we don't want rescuing a teammate to feel like just another task. We want it to be a rewarding part of working together as a squad, where lending a hand really makes a difference."

Q3: If I'm still missing some Collectibles when S1 ends, will I get another chance to collect them?

You will! We've got new gameplay coming in the second half of S1, giving you more reliable ways to get Collectibles. And even after the season wraps up, we'll bring back Collectibles from previous seasons through future events, so you'll still have plenty of chances to fill in the gaps.

Q4: Chaos Mode feels way too punishing right now. I always get knocked, and there aren't many viable Aniimo or team comps to choose from. Any plans to improve it?

Chaos Mode is meant to be the toughest challenge in squad-based Operation: Egg Heist, where greater risks come with greater rewards. But we don't want higher difficulty to simply mean getting knocked down more often. We want you to have more ways to deal with danger, adapt to different situations, and find strategies that work for you. With that in mind, here's what we're planning based on your feedback:

1. More team composition options We're adding more Aniimo suited to Operation: Egg Heist, opening up new team compositions and strategies for you to experiment with. Keep an eye out for new Aniimo in upcoming updates!

2. More Chip acquisition methods We'll gradually introduce more ways to obtain Chips, including new sources for Heal Chips and Chips that improve the melee combat experience.

3. More ways to tackle challenges in the Sanctum We're planning to introduce more interactive gameplay elements throughout the Sanctum. Like by activating certain mechanisms or defeating specific Aniimo, you'll be able to gain temporary abilities that help you adapt to different combat situations.

4. A more flexible approach to high-difficulty challenges Going forward, high-difficulty content will tend to follow a format similar to the current Limited-Time Challenge, with reasonable rewards. You'll be free to choose whether to take part."

Q5: What's the update plan for Operation: Egg Heist, and how often can we expect new content?

We'll be rolling out major updates each season, alongside smaller updates every two weeks to keep things fresh. Here's a look:

First half of the season: Updates will focus primarily on PvE content. Second half of the season: We'll shift our focus to casual competitive modes. Fresh content every half-season: We'll introduce new Collectibles, along with new maps, Aniimo, and gameplays. Small updates every two weeks: Smaller updates will bring new content, including new Aniimo and their drops, as well as balance tweaks and other adjustments. New Alphas and mobs with unique mechanics: These new foes will bring more variety to combat with their own unique mechanics, and we'll introduce exclusive challenge rewards to go with them.

By combining major seasonal updates with smaller updates every two weeks, we want each stage of Operation: Egg Heist to feel fresh, while giving you new things to collect and new challenges to take on throughout.

Q6: Why doesn't increasing ATK always mean more damage for certain Aniimo?

We believe an Aniimo's role should reflect its specialty in combat, not limit how you choose to train it. Even if an Aniimo isn't particularly good at dealing damage, we still want you to be able to bring it into battle, make the most of its strengths, and enjoy experimenting with different builds. To make this possible, we've built a safeguard into the damage calculation for non-DPS Aniimo. When their ATK is low, they receive an ATK boost based on their level (or their BREAK stat, for BREAK Aniimo) when damage is calculated. This ensures they can still break through enemy defenses rather than struggle to deal damage at all. However, this safeguard comes with a downside. When an Aniimo's ATK falls below the guaranteed minimum, investing more in ATK won't immediately translate into higher damage. This explains why some of you have noticed that your Aniimo's damage stays the same even after boosting its ATK.We understand how confusing this can be. After all, investing in a stat should feel rewarding! That's why we're planning to refine the damage calculation in Version 1.1, so that ATK increases have a more direct impact on damage while keeping the overall combat experience largely unchanged. We'll share the details in an official announcement ahead of the update.

And that wraps up this edition of Dev Feedback, dedicated to Operation: Egg Heist.

Feel free to leave any other questions. We look forward to hearing from you and answering more of them in the future.

The Aniimo Dev Team

items.content:
Dear Pathfinders,

Hello everyone! Since Aniimo launched, we’ve been blown away by your love and support. Thank you so much for stepping into Idyll and setting out on this adventure with us. Every hour you play and every kind word you share is what motivates us to keep going.

At the same time, we’ve seen plenty of honest feedback and complaints. Every suggestion, complaint, and question you post on social media, in comment sections, and in community is read and reviewed by our dev team. To us, such feedback shows that you genuinely love Aniimo and want it to get better.

Every so often, we’ll round up the issues you care about and talk about most, and share with you what we think, what we’re changing, and what’s coming next. Here are the top issues this time, along with our progress and plans:

1. Rerolling the same Aniimo keeps giving repeat colors and burns through resources. Can this be improved?

In version 1.1, we’re improving Sparkling Hue rerolls for Sparkling Prismana Aniimo. Once it’s live, you’ll be able to freely switch between any Sparkling Hue you’ve already unlocked for an Aniimo.

2. Some Aniimo already look great in their original Prismana colors. After using a Sparkling Cube, can I keep the original color?

After the version 1.1 update, you’ll be able to switch between all the Sparkling Hue styles unlocked for that Prismana Aniimo, including its original Prismana Hue, so you can switch back any time.

3. Why does my Legendary Irisalis have 88 Potential when someone else’s has 99?

We’ve read through all your feedback. Right now, Irisalis’s Innate Potential is random. Since you can only get this Legendary Aniimo once, having random Potential means the payoff isn’t guaranteed for this rare Aniimo. That’s not the experience we want for you.

So after the version 1.1 update, we’re removing Irisalis’s random Innate Potential and setting it to fixed values: ATK: 10, REGEN: 10, HP: 5, BREAK: 5, M.DEF: 5, P.DEF: 5

Any existing Potential above these values will be converted into Starcryst Essence as compensation. Watch for the version update announcement and in-game mail for the exact conversion rules and amounts.

4. Can I switch a Sparkling Aniimo I already own to a Legendary Aniipod’s exclusive Sparkling effect?

After the version 1.1 update, Legendary Aniipods can be used on Sparkling Aniimo. This replaces the Aniipod it was originally caught with and grants that Legendary Aniipod’s exclusive Sparkling effect.

5. Are there plans to fix lag and overheating on mobile?

We’ve received a lot of feedback on this. A dedicated team is optimizing for popular devices right now to reduce lag and overheating and improve the mobile experience as soon as possible.

6. Support tickets take a long time to get a reply. Can this be faster?

We’re continuing to improve how support works, including upgrading the support system, growing the team, and streamlining internal handoffs so that tickets get answered and resolved faster. Some complex issues require checking account data and working across several teams to find the cause, so they may take longer, but we’ll keep improving. Thank you for your patience and understanding.

7. My Steam/Console account failed to link. What should I do?

Please log in to our Customer Support page.

Under Quick Support Links, click Account Issues. Then select Steam Relink (PSN/Xbox) for both the second-level and third-level categories.

Please submit a support ticket with the following information:

- The platform ID you would like to unlink (e.g., Steam ID)

- The UID you are currently using to contact Customer Support, along with the email address linked to it

- The UID you would like to unlink

- The platform currently linked to the UID you would like to unlink

We will review your request and process it as soon as possible.

We’ll keep reviewing your real experiences and suggestions, and share bug fixes, improvements, mechanic changes, and future plans openly. We’d love to hear more of your feedback, too.

Thank you again to every Pathfinder for your patience and honest feedback. Every message you leave motivates us to keep improving. Have fun and enjoy your time in Idyll!

The Aniimo Dev Team

A week after its PC and console debut on September 16, Aniimo has made it to iOS and Android. The mobile launch of Pawprint Studio's open-world creature-catching RPG isn't a separate product bolted onto the original; link an Aniimo Pass account and the same save follows you across mobile, PC (Steam and Epic Games Store), PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X|S, with cross-play tying all of it together.

Pathfinders is what Pawprint Studio calls its players, and Idyll is where they play. The mechanic holding the game together is Twine, which lets a Pathfinder essentially borrow traits from any of over 200 Aniimo species : their movement, mostly, which opens up terrain that's otherwise off-limits, but also combat moves specific to that species. More than 40 million people pre-registered before any of this went live. On the question of whether mobile got a lesser version of the game, Pawprint Studio's answer is no. Egg Heist survived the jump intact, and so did Homeland, the base-building system that shipped with the original release.

One thing sets the mobile build apart: an Obsidian Aniimo variant that PC and console players simply don't have access to. As for rewards, Pawprint Studio tied its biggest one to actual progress rather than showing up every day, so hitting the Junior Wayfarer milestone earns a free Prismana-form Aniimo , chosen by the player. Catching items and cosmetics from ongoing events come on top. Touch controls and gamepad support were each tuned separately for mobile, and the voice acting now covers more languages than it did at launch.

Storage-wise, budget around 18GB on Android , which also needs Vulkan 1.1, a Snapdragon 855 or Dimensity 1000 chip at the low end, 6GB RAM, and Android 10 to run. iOS asks for similar storage, an iPhone 11 or newer, and iOS 16. Progression carries over fully between platforms, so nobody switching to their phone from PC or console has to start their collection over.

items.title: 'Aniimo' Launches Globally on Mobile, Expanding to All Platforms
items.summary: Pawprint Studio has launched the mobile version of its open-world creature-catching RPG Aniimo globally, expanding supported platforms to iOS and Android.
items.content:
Korean (한국어) KO Add us on Pawprint Studio has launched the mobile version of its open-world creature-catching RPG Aniimo globally, expanding supported platforms to iOS and Android. Global pre-registrations surpassed 40 million, while peak concurrent users on Steam reached 168,000.

Aniimo is available on mobile, its official website, Steam, Epic Games Store, and PS5 and Xbox console versions. Supporting cross-progression and cross-play across platforms, the game ranked 4th on South Korea's Steam top sellers chart following its PC and console launch on September 16. Its official Discord community has surpassed 150,000 members, and it holds a Metacritic score of 78.

The core system, "Twine," allows players to merge with Aniimo to utilize their unique abilities. Players can observe the world through an Aniimo's perspective, explore hidden areas and underground spaces, or blend into specific packs to discover side stories and species-specific lore. During the catching process, players can lower a monster's health in combat, as well as approach from behind or lure them with bait.

Increasing field exploration unlocks "Ecosystem Nurture" content, allowing players to induce "Wild Surges" where large numbers of Aniimo appear in specific areas. Rare "Prismana" variants with different appearances and colors appear at a set probability, and a new "Obsidian" form has been added to the mobile version.

The game features over 200 species of Aniimo. Each creature features distinct material rendering based on its characteristics, such as fur, metal, and liquid, while weather and day-night cycles, field puzzles, and species-specific behavioral patterns shape the environment of the continent of Idyll.

For multiplayer content, the game offers "Egg Scramble," a PvPvE mode combining competition and cooperation. It also supports lifestyle features encompassing collection, catching, growth, competition, and social play, including housing and "RV Camps" for interacting with other users.

During the launch month, an event will boost the spawn rate of Prismana variants and allow players to select a Prismana Aniimo of their choice. In South Korea, a collaboration with No Brand Burger begins on October 2, featuring a mascot Susuta costume photo zone and on-site events at participating locations.

Future updates will run on an 84-day seasonal model. Content will be added by splitting each season into a 42-day first half and second half, introducing a new water-themed region, five new islands, and uncharted territories. New Aniimo, "Sparkling Aniimo" variants, and cosmetic content will also be added sequentially.

Currently, full Korean voice acting is applied to the main story. Pawprint Studio plans to continuously improve the quality of Korean localization, including translation and voiceover work.

The Pawprint Studio development team stated, "Following PC and consoles, we are delighted to bring Aniimo to mobile and embark on adventures across the continent of Idyll with even more players. We will continue to consistently add new Aniimo, regions, and diverse content while listening closely to feedback from Korean players to deliver an even more refined gameplay experience."

Could this be the next Palworld to offer players an alternative to Pokémon?

Aniimo is a new open-world creature-catching RPG from Chinese developer Pawprint Studio. In the game, you explore a vast world and throw cubes at wild Aniimo to catch them before using the creatures in battle. Sounds a lot like Pokémon , right?

However, Aniimo puts its own spin on the familiar formula by allowing players to transform into their creatures. You can then directly control them to explore the world, complete traversal sections and solve puzzles.

Like Palworld , Aniimo appears to offer a fresh take on the catch ’em all genre. Despite only launching today, September 16, the game is already a hit on PC. According to SteamDB , Aniimo has surpassed 101,717 peak concurrent players on Steam . Considering it is still early morning across much of North America, that is pretty impressive!

It is difficult to say whether this will be the next Palworld , but Aniimo has already impressed Pokémon fans with its gorgeous visuals. However, despite its promising player count, not everyone is enjoying the new creature-catching RPG.

At the time of writing, Aniimo has a “Mixed” user rating on Steam. One of the biggest complaints is that the game reportedly adopts a gacha-like structure after its opening tutorial, with microtransactions and paid options that can speed up progression.

“Has such potential. Very good graphics, cool design of aniimo. However about an hour into the game you are bombarded with monthly passes, stores, objectives that you can bypass by paying, ways to speed up your levelling. Its very much a gatcha game,” one Steam user review reads. Another frustrated reviewer wrote: “Aniimo promised an authentic, gacha-free creature collector, but it delivers nothing more than a glorified digital storefront.”

It should be pointed out that the game does not require players to purchase these items. Not every review has been negative, either. One player wrote: “Im already loving how cute the aniimo and everything about this game is. It’s basically Palworld + Infinity Nikki! ”

While its Steam reviews are currently mixed, Aniimo is already off to a strong start based on how many people are playing it. Even if it does not reach the ridiculous heights of Palworld , this is another example of how much demand there is for new Pokémon-like games. And with Pokémon Winds and Waves still around a year and a half away, I totally get it.

No, Aniimo is not a gacha game . Despite having all the bells and whistles a gacha usually throws at us—including about a thousand currencies and menus to stress over—Aniimo doesn't have any banner systems that gacha games like Genshin Impact or Infinity Nikki do.

All Aniimo, their equipment, Aniimo eggs, and anything related to cute critter combat and fashion is not linked to random odds, or reaching an arbitrary "pity" number that eventually guarantees something after enough pulls. You get Aniimo (and most other items) just by playing the game, seriously, and instead most (but not all) cosmetics are linked to coughing up a fixed amount of cash in the store.

That's because Aniimo did have a gacha system, but only during its final beta. The Rift Exploration event—AKA a banner—was a very sneaky inclusion, because these rifts involved spending a premium currency for the chance to catch a Legendary Aniimo by filling up a bar, not pulling on a banner with a button press.

It didn't look like your regular banner system, but the capture rate for the Legendary Aniimo was so miniscule that unless you got very lucky, you probably had to rely on reaching "pity" to finally guarantee catching it—just like a banner in any other gacha.

Yet another Pokémon-inspired game is popping off on Steam, with over 160,000 concurrent players for Aniimo HoYoverse's Nodusfall is free to play but isn't a typical gacha game: 'Characters are not obtained through random draws' All active Aniimo codes for launch, September 2026 Rift Exploration was very poorly received by beta testers and future players alike. The rifts reportedly got stale and repetitive real quick, plus, lots of people pointed out the developers had promised many times that Aniimo wouldn't be locked behind gacha. For Aniimo's full launch, Rift Exploration has been replaced with a token collection system.

Developer Pawprint Studio never mentioned Rift Explorations were changed because of the gacha backlash in the official blog post , but I'm willing to gamble (one last time) that it sure contributed to the change.

Then how is Aniimo trying to get my money? As a free-to-play live service game, Aniimo is of course still trying to shake down your wallet, even without a gacha system. Its monetization model of choice is a cosmetics shop where you convert real life money into Lumin Crystals, then exchange that currency for outfits and accessories for your playable character and Aniimo. Some cosmetics are available for free by using one of the other in-game currencies, but the coolest and cutest sets will inevitably be locked behind a paywall.

Another "give us your money" tactic is Aniimo's shop bundles , which asks for Lumin Crystals (your real money) in exchange for Aniipods, profile backgrounds, Aniimo stat alterations, guaranteed ways to get rare versions of Aniimo, or other types of currency. You can still get some of these items by spending the Glimmer or Credits currency instead, or from rewards by just playing the game, but you bet they're far harder to get this way.

Then there's the inevitable battle pass , which Aniimo calls a "Companion Handbook" (for twee capitalism purposes, I guess). A free tier is unlocked automatically, but two premium tracks include extra goodies, including Aniimo, cosmetics, and a fast-track to higher battle pass levels.

items.title: Aniimo Launches Today – Begin Your Journey into Idyll
items.summary: The moment creature-collecting fans have been waiting for is finally here. The team here at Pawprint Studio is delighted to see Aniimo officially launch
items.content:
The moment creature-collecting fans have been waiting for is finally here. The team here at Pawprint Studio is delighted to see Aniimo officially launch today, bringing the vibrant world of Idyll and its adorable creatures, the Aniimo, to players around the world. This is the chance for all of us to finally jump into the adventure, explore diverse regions, and discover the Aniimo who thrive across Idyll’s unique biomes.

First, we want to thank all the players who participated in our beta tests and shared feedback on gameplay, mechanics, and features. Your support and insights have helped us shape the game and reach the moment we have all been waiting for – global launch! I wanted to share with you how this feedback has contributed to the game’s development and what new additions you can expect to encounter!

At launch, players will be able to discover, meet, and collect more than 200 Aniimo. Among the newest additions are Squarrel and its evolution, Squashel. This energetic squirrel-like Aniimo rolls down hillsides while clutching its tail and attacks using fast-paced combo mechanics centered around its powerful tail abilities. It is a unique addition to the Aniimo roster and we think that players will have a lot of fun with it!

Following important feedback from our pioneering Pathfinders, we redesigned the entire Irisalis encounter flow across three key areas: capture, gameplay experience, and the encounter ritual itself. This updated structure will also serve as the foundation for future Legendary Aniimo events, creating a smoother and more intuitive experience for players. Again, we’re grateful for the feedback on this gameplay sequence which has had a profound impact on how we view these events.

We have also improved the way Pathfinders train and level up their Aniimo. Updates include a simplified Held Item System, increased Star Dust drop rates, and progression caps that now unlock naturally alongside an Aniimo’s level progression.

We refined the overall level progression and upgrade experience within Homeland gameplay, while also expanding the map with additional features, activities, and interactive elements for Pathfinders to explore and enjoy.

Additionally, we’ve optimized controls for both mobile devices and gamepads to deliver a smoother experience across all platforms. We’ve also added multilingual voice acting to the main storyline and improved translation quality across all supported languages, creating a more immersive and seamless gameplay experience for players worldwide.

These improvements are only the beginning. Our goal at Pawprint Studio is to create a fun and exciting creature-collecting experience that players can enjoy for years to come, and your feedback will continue to help shape the future of Aniimo . We are truly grateful for all the support and passion you have shown throughout every stage of bringing Aniimo to life.

Whether you are stepping into the world of Aniimo for the very first time or have been following our journey from the beginning, the gates to Idyll are finally opening. We’re excited to welcome you into this magical universe and invite you to become part of the adventure. Join us on XBOX Series X|S, XBOX PC, and XBOX Game Pass today.

For the latest updates on Aniimo , upcoming events, and future content, visit www.aniimo.com and follow our community channels . Join the community and continue your journey through the world of Idyll with fellow Pathfinders around the globe.

items.title: Aniimo Release Date Countdown & Exact Start Times
items.summary: All the details on the release date for Aniimo, including the exact start time you can jump in to the free-to-play creature-capture.
items.content:
September is when releases start to come thick and fast for gamers, and among those due to land in the coming weeks is Aniimo, with the release date and start time nailed on.

Aniimo is a new creature-capture title from Pawprint Studio releasing for free across multiple platforms, putting players into a world where they can transform into the creatures they capture.

If you’re keen to dive into Aniimo the moment it launches and want all the details, Insider Gaming has you covered.

Aniimo is slated for launch on September 16 across the main slew of devices, followed by a subsequent mobile launch later this month on September 23.

At the initial launch, Aniimo will be available on PC, PlayStation 5, and XBOX Series X|S, with the free-to-play nature of the game meaning you won’t have to splash out any additional funds to purchase the title.

However, some pre-order bonuses are available, but that’s entirely up to you, and there’s no early access period either, so all players will land at the same time.

Having said that, the exact date does depend on where you are located in the world, as some players will be able to jump in a day earlier.

Aniimo is slated for release at 10 AM in China on September 16, which means that players in the United States can jump into the title on September 15.

With a global release schedule, the doors will open worldwide for all players simultaneously, and time zone differences mean those in the US can play in the evening of September 15.

The start time is confirmed by both the official PlayStation website and SteamDB , so the start times should be concrete and not subject to any changes.
